title: Qwen's outputs into the training data, kept apart by answerer; Claude's stay evaluation only and silver
request: Step 3 of the Qwen switch plan: record the owner's decision that OpenRouter Qwen's outputs and reasoning may be stored and trained on (weight 1.0, source class open_weights_model, licence checked before any fine-tune); let the lake harvest keep model-role answers of every served model under an answerer per model (Claude eval_only, Qwen train); route OpenRouter Qwen exchanges and trajectories in the store to their own folders at full weight, not frontier silver; fixture tests only.
spec: the Qwen switch plan (magical-waddling-honey), step 3; docs/guides/TRAINING_DATA_FACTORY_PLAN.md (source class and licence check before a fine-tune)
plan: Read owner_decisions.json and provider_outputs.py, the harvest's per-answerer views, answers.ANSWERERS, dclab_core/lake.py EVAL_ONLY and the store's answerer_of and folder routing.
Put the one rule of which model falls under the decision in provider_outputs.py, used by both the lake and the store.
Tie each model-role answer to the model of its own request where its exchange is kept; fall back on the workspace's models.
Add Qwen folders in the store beside Claude's silver ones, consent from the owner's record.
Fixture tests for each, the store and lake suites, make store-check, then the reviewer.

decisions.decision: Name-only fallback counts only OpenRouter's lower-case slug (qwen/..., openrouter/qwen/...); the exchange's provider and source_class win when present.
decisions.why: A Hugging Face id (Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct:novita) is another host's and an Ollama tag runs locally; the owner's words are about OpenRouter Qwen only. Step 2 adds the labels, so the name rule only covers older exchanges.

decisions.decision: Models other than Claude and OpenRouter Qwen are kept under their own answerer with use eval_only.
decisions.why: Their terms or licence are not checked; keeping them (instead of skipping) loses nothing and one decision can promote them later.

decisions.decision: Qwen's store folders are apart (trajectories/openrouter_qwen, reasoning/openrouter_qwen, reasoning/final_turn_openrouter_qwen), not the clean sets.
decisions.why: Kept apart by answerer so one change of owner_decisions.json takes them out (tested: consent becomes improve).

decisions.decision: A Qwen run that a provider's model (Claude) helped is mixed and silver; a rules run Qwen helped goes to Qwen's folder.
decisions.why: Claude's words must never reach a full-weight training row.
Qwen's answers come from the sessions it served (harvest); capture loads a local GLiNER model and would fail or mislabel.

change: owner_decisions.json gains openrouter_qwen. provider_outputs.py gains decision= on for_training and consent, weight(), openrouter_qwen() and answerer_name(). lake/harvest.py: request_models() reads the kept exchanges for the request ids model-role answers carry; served_times() gives every model ever served with its time; model_of() picks the exact request, else the models served ten minutes before the decision, else every model ever served (Claude among them wins); answerer_for() files Claude eval_only, OpenRouter Qwen train, others eval_only; shadow model-role answers go under their own model; sealed places (exam_vault, sealed) never give a training row; twin AI-first lanes read the model field or the expert answerer's prefix; the rebuild clears sessions and twin under every answerer folder. lake/answers.py: a hosted qwen3.8-flash entry and a refusal in capture(). store/sets/llm.py: answerer_of returns openrouter:<model>; open_weights, silver_of, exchange_answerer, qwen_weight; three Qwen folders with their abouts and consent; from_exchange keeps provider and source_class in check; intern weights and mixed helpers. Tests in five files.

findings.defect: Claude's pre-switch model-role answers were filed under qwen3.8-flash with use train.
findings.scenario: A workspace served home_agent by Claude on 2026-10-17 and by Qwen on 2026-11-11; a model-role answer with no request id (most roles pass none) is harvested.
findings.cause: The fallback read served_models, which keeps only the latest model per purpose, so after the switch it saw one model: Qwen.
findings.fix: served_times() keeps every ok request with its time; model_of() uses the models served in the ten minutes before the decision, then every model ever served, Claude among them winning.

findings.defect: A shadow model's model-role answer was attributed to the served model first, then moved to dclab-classifiers.
findings.scenario: A Qwen workspace keeps {by: model_role, answerer: shadow:ollama:qwen3.5:4b, source: shadow}.
findings.cause: model_of ran before the shadow override and the override renamed every shadow answer as a classifier's.
findings.fix: A model-role shadow answer is filed under its own model's name (eval_only unless it is OpenRouter Qwen); the classifier override applies to non-model-role shadows only.

findings.defect: Twin AI-first lanes Qwen ran were filed as Claude's.
findings.scenario: twin/home.py writes answerer ai_first@home with the model apart; twin/compare.py writes ai_first@expert:qwen/qwen3.8-flash.
findings.cause: The rule read the answerer field only.
findings.fix: _ai_first_model reads model, else the expert prefix, else the answerer.

findings.defect: A sealed run's Qwen model answers could become training rows.
findings.scenario: A future sealed exam on Qwen whose workspace under agent_runs/exam_vault keeps model_requests.jsonl.
findings.cause: The harvest walks all of agent_runs, sealed folders included; before the switch such answers were Claude's and eval_only anyway.
findings.fix: sealed_place(): a record found under exam_vault or a sealed folder, or a twin run there, never gets use train for a model answer.

findings.defect: Name-only matching could claim another host's lower-case qwen/... id (Groq's qwen/qwen3-32b) on an exchange kept before step 2.
findings.scenario: An old exchange with no provider field from a non-OpenRouter host using a lower-case qwen/ slug.
findings.cause: Without the gateway's labels only the name is known.
findings.fix: None: after step 2 the provider decides; the weights are open either way. Kept as a known risk.

measurements.name: touched test files
measurements.result: Five changed files: 59 tests pass after the review's fixes (56 before them).

measurements.name: store and lake suites
measurements.gate: Every store, lake, archive and provider_outputs test file passes.
measurements.result: 50 files, 337 tests OK before the fixes; the 9 most related files (103 tests) OK after them.

measurements.name: make store-check
measurements.result: passed 30 of 30 (before the review's fixes, which touch the lake only).

outcome: OpenRouter Qwen's answers and reasoning reach training data under their own answerer and folders at full weight, by the owner's recorded decision; Claude's stay evaluation only in the lake and silver in the store. Nothing committed (the tree is shared with the other steps' sessions). Not run on the real workspaces: make capture and the store run happen in step 4.
lessons: A 'latest model per purpose' summary is wrong for attribution across a provider switch: keep every request with its time.
Read every writer of a field (twin home and compare both write ai_first) before reading it; they named the model in three different places.
risks: Most roles still record no request id on their model-role answers; the ten-minute window can file an answer as unknown-model when several non-Claude models serve one workspace at once.
Qwen's licence and OpenRouter's terms are not yet checked; that check is required before any fine-tune uses these sets.
A local Ollama model is eval_only in the lake but clean (train) in the store: a policy difference left for the owner.
